note: Set A's four claims are all clean and faithful: the plywood deck, hex through bolt, reclaimed wood surface and frame sizes are read and bound exactly as labeled. Set B recovers a few extra facts (bolt diameter/length, fastener type, reclaimed-wood material) but states most of them redundantly under two names (frame 'nominal size' vs 'dimensions', 'hex through bolt dimensions' vs 'through bolt size', 'deck surface' thickness/width vs 'reclaimed wood surface' dimensions, plywood deck split three ways) and adds one unsupported claim binding the graphic-scale label 1/2" as a dimension of the deck module connection. B also uses vaguer entities ('through bolt', 'deck surface', 'fasteners', 'frame') where the page gives specific labels. On balance A is the more correct and faithful set despite being thinner.
remarks: Both sets omit the 2" X 8" JOIST callout, which appears twice in the text layer and is an important component fact. The trailing numbers in the text layer (0, 1", 2", 4", 3", 0, 1', 1 1/2', 1/2") are graphic scale-bar labels, not component dimensions; extraction should suppress them or bind them only to the scale bars. B's splitting of a single 'A x B' callout into separate thickness/width claims is acceptable in principle but here duplicates the full dimension claim under a different entity name.
